title: DECISION: iterative DP wildmat avoids ReDoS
description: The wildmat matching engine (wildmat.rs) uses an iterative O(n*m) dynamic programming table instead of recursive backtracking. Recursive backtracking on patterns like '*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a*a' against long non-matching strings produces exponential (2^n) blowup — a ReDoS class attack. The DP approach fills a (text.len()+1)*(pattern.len()+1) boolean table in one pass, bounding worst-case time to O(n*m) regardless of pattern adversarialness. This is the correct algorithm for wildcard matching in a network-facing service where patterns come from operator config and names come from untrusted peers.
